q: Which of the following is used in tilt and turn windows, allowing the sash to tilt inward at the top or swing fully open like a door?
n: Figure E is tilt-and-turn hardware: one handle tilts the sash inward at the top for ventilation or swings it fully open like a door. Source: Window hardware manufacturer literature (Roto, Siegenia).

q: Which of the following is used in swing windows, allowing the window sash to open inward or outward on side hinges?
n: Figure B is the casement handle and hinge set for side-hinged swing windows that open inward or outward. Source: Window hardware manufacturer literature.

q: Which of the following is used in jalousie windows, allowing multiple glass slats to open and close simultaneously for ventilation?
n: Figure A is the jalousie operator, a lever or crank linked to all the slats so they open and close together. Source: Window hardware manufacturer literature.

q: Which of the following is used in awning windows, allowing the window to swing outward from the bottom, hinged at the top?
n: Figure D is the friction stay used on awning windows, which are hinged at the top and swing out at the bottom. Source: Window hardware manufacturer literature.

q: Which hardware can be used for a wooden window?
n: Figure A is hardware for wooden windows, fixed with wood screws into the timber sash and frame. Source: Window hardware manufacturer literature.

q: Which hardware can be used for screen windows?
n: Figure B, the light roller, is used on sliding screen windows. Source: Window hardware manufacturer literature.

q: Which hardware can be used for a uPVC window?
n: uPVC windows use profile-specific hardware: Figure C (sliding rollers) and Figure D (friction stays), set into the reinforced uPVC chambers. Source: uPVC window manufacturer literature.

q: Which hardware can be used for an aluminum window?
n: Aluminum windows use friction stays (Figure D) and sliding cam locks (Figure E), both made for aluminum profiles. Source: Aluminum window manufacturer literature.

q: Which hardware can be used for a curtain wall window?
n: Curtain wall vents are top-hung and use heavy-duty friction stays (Figure D). Source: Curtain wall manufacturer literature.

q: Which window keeps rain out while still letting air in during a downpour?
n: An awning window is hinged at the top, so the open sash acts like a hood that sheds rain while air still comes in below it. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (window types).

q: Which type of window admits up to 95% of air?
n: Louvers with wide (about 150 mm) blades open almost the whole window area, so they admit up to about 95% of the opening's airflow, more than sliders (about 50%). Source: Window manufacturer ventilation data; Olgyay, Design with Climate.

q: Which type of window is the easiest to clean?
n: A casement opens fully on side hinges (often with extension hinges), so both faces of the glass can be reached from inside for cleaning. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; window manufacturer literature.

q: Which window is hardest to reach?
n: Clerestory windows are set high in the wall above eye level, so they are the hardest to reach for operation and cleaning. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: Which type of window is best for a kitchen that opens onto a lanai?
n: A sliding window opens wide as a pass-through from kitchen to lanai, with no sash swinging into the counter or the outdoor area. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated; Time-Saver Standards (residential).

q: Which type of window is commonly used in condominiums where safety and waterproofing are important?
n: In condominiums, awning windows open only partially at the bottom, which limits falls, while the top hinge keeps rain out. That makes them a safe, weathertight choice for high floors. Source: Window manufacturer literature; NBC IRR Rule VIII (openings).

q: Which window is common in shower areas?
n: Small high awning windows are common in shower areas: they vent humid air and give privacy, and the top-hinged sash keeps water out. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which window gives the best natural ventilation?
n: Jalousie windows open nearly the full area of the opening and their angled slats direct breezes, so they give the best natural ventilation of the choices. Source: Olgyay, Design with Climate; window manufacturer ventilation data.

q: Which type of window is commonly used in hospitals?
n: Sliding windows are common in hospitals: they do not project into corridors or outside, are easy to secure with limiters and are simple to clean. Source: DOH Planning and Design Guidelines for Hospitals; Time-Saver Standards (hospitals).

q: Which window should NOT open onto a hallway?
n: An outward-opening casement onto a hallway would swing into people's path and is a hazard. Sliding, picture and louver windows stay within the wall plane. Source: NBC IRR Rule XII (exits and corridors); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: What is a long horizontal band of windows called?
n: A ribbon window is a continuous horizontal band of windows, one of Le Corbusier's Five Points of Architecture. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture; Le Corbusier, Five Points of a New Architecture (1926).

q: A high-rise condo uses mostly fixed windows with small openings for safety. What does this give up?
n: Fixed windows keep the view and are safe, but they give up comfort because the small openings severely limit natural ventilation. Source: Philippine Green Building Code (2015), natural ventilation; Olgyay, Design with Climate.

q: What fills the space between the panes of double-glazed windows?
n: Double-glazed units have a sealed space filled with dehydrated air or an inert gas such as argon, which slows heat and sound transfer. Source: ASTM E2190 (insulating glass units).

q: Which type of window is best for tropical countries to allow maximum airflow?
n: A casement opens almost 100% of its area, and the open sash scoops passing breezes into the room, so it is a strong choice for tropical airflow. Source: Olgyay, Design with Climate; Philippine Green Building Code (2015).

q: What is the proper way to install a steel window frame?
o: Either way, depending on the installer
Finish the opening first, then set the frame
Set the frame before finishing the opening
n: Steel window frames are set, anchored and grouted into the rough opening first, and the opening is then plastered and finished around them for a tight, sealed fit. Source: Philippine construction practice; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which window is hinged at the top?
n: An awning window is hinged at the top and swings outward at the bottom. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (window types).

q: Which window is hinged at the side?
n: A casement window is hinged at the side and swings like a door. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (window types).

q: Which window has adjustable horizontal glass slats?
n: A jalousie window has horizontal glass slats on a common operator that all tilt together. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: Which window runs on a horizontal track and doesn't project in or out?
n: A sliding window runs on a horizontal track and stays in the wall plane, projecting neither in nor out. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (window types).

q: Which window is fixed and cannot open?
n: A picture window is a large fixed pane that cannot open. It frames a view. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.

q: What is the main disadvantage of wooden windows?
o: They shrink and swell with the weather
n: Wood absorbs and loses moisture, so wooden windows shrink and swell with the weather, sticking in wet seasons and leaving gaps in dry ones. Source: US Forest Service, Wood Handbook (dimensional change).

q: What is the main reason why jalousie windows are popular?
n: Jalousies remain popular mainly because they are cheap: standard glass blades and a simple operator cost much less than casement or sliding units. Source: Philippine window supplier price lists; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which window looks cheaper because it uses ordinary hinges?
n: A wood casement hung on ordinary butt hinges has a plain, utilitarian look and appears cheaper than aluminum units with concealed hardware. Source: Window manufacturer literature.

q: Which window is most likely to leak air without maintenance?
n: Jalousie blades only overlap and never seal tightly, so they leak air (and dust and rain) more than other windows, especially as the clips wear. Source: AAMA air infiltration testing; Olgyay, Design with Climate.

q: Which type of window is least recommended for areas exposed to strong winds?
n: Jalousie windows are weakest in strong winds: the overlapping blades let wind-driven rain in and can be blown out of their clips during typhoons. Source: Window manufacturer literature; Philippine typhoon-resistant housing guidelines.
